english.title: Designer or manufacturer of work product/fairground equipment fail to carry out health and safety research

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Health and Safety at Work Act 1974

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person who undertook the

(A)_[design]_
(B)_[manufacture]_

of an article

(C)_[for use at work,]_
(D)_[of fairground equipment,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..), failed to discharge your duty to carry out or arrange for the carrying out of necessary research with a view to the discovery and, so far as was reasonably practicable, the elimination or minimisation of risks to health or safety to which the

(E)_[design]_
(F)_[article]_

may have given rise
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6(2) and 33(1)(a) of, and Schedule 3A to, the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
undertook design / manufacture of article for use at work / fairground equipment
fail to carry out / arrange for carrying out of necessary research
with view to discovery and elimination / minimisation of risks to health or safety

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 2(2) of the Act for examples of the extent of the employer's duty.
(ii) Proceedings for an offence shall not, in England and Wales, be instituted except by an inspector of the Environment Agency or the Natural Resources Body for Wales or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, see section 38 of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see Schedule 3A to the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
